effect: AI countries now raise defence spending in earnest at war. The AI's defence budget closed 2.4 to 4.5% of the gap to its target a month (half-life 15 to 28 months), whether or not it was at war, and its target had no term for survival, so an invaded state drifted up a few points of GDP over years where Ukraine went from about 3% to about 30% within a year. While actually fighting (the game's active-hostilities flag, so not in a ceasefire or armistice) the budget now closes the gap up to about three times faster (quarterly rate up to 25% plus competence, against 7%), and the target rises by 2 points of GDP plus 60 points per unit of population occupied, at most 15: a country with a tenth of its people occupied aims about 8 points higher. Both extras halve every three years of the most recent war the country is actively fighting (ceasefires keep a war's start date and do not reset it), so a long war settles back instead of sustaining itself; a new war, even a small one, brings the effort back. A war already years old at the start counts those years. Peace returns to the old pace. The game's own ceiling on the line still applies. The sizes are a tuning choice, nearer Russia's about 3 to 7% than Ukraine's about 30%, which this cap cannot reach by itself. Expected effect: invaded AI states fight harder and spend more, with more deficits and debt; a default risk is possible and is on the watch list. Day 0: seeded wars start moving from the first month. No new state. (Minified names in this text are those of build 26403824; the patch's find text has the current ones.)
